content.title: How much are the cheapest last-minute Coachella 2026 tickets?
content.text: Getty Images It’s almost time to make the annual pilgrimage to Indio. Starting Friday, April 10, the first weekend of Coachella gets underway at the Empire Polo Field. Big names set to grace the seven Cali stages include short n’ sweet singer Sabrina Carpenter, mysterious pop icon Justin Bieber, party-starting hit-maker Karol G, ’00s rockers The Strokes and beat-dropping turntablist Anyma. Elder Millennials and Gen X-ers in attendance will likely be pleased to see throwback heroes Iggy Pop, David Byrne, Moby, DEVO and Suicidal Tendencies on the bill as well. Rounding out the expansive lineup are Turnstile, KATSEYE, Sombr, Blood Orange and Teddy Swims. All in all, there are 140 artists set to perform. Fans hoping to catch them all live can still snag last-minute tickets before time runs out. At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on tickets for weekend one three-day passes was $1,437 including fees on StubHub. Single-day weekend one passes start at $812 including fees. For those hoping to swing into Coachella on weekend two, multi-day passes can be found for as low as $812 including fees. In addition to all the exciting acts set to perform, the annual fest also offers an activities tent (with lip sync challenges, water balloon fights, pickleball, human ring toss), a camp lounge (where you can watch morning cartoons and video games), Coachella Art Studios, a “Euphoria” season 3 screening and a miniaturized version of Coachella you have to see to believe. Plus, the famous ferris wheel, a speaker series, a polar bear dating game, a Radiohead film screening and shopping will be on site as well. Notable food on the premises include massive ice cream sandwiches from Afters, hand pulled Bang Bang Noodles, mouth watering Birrieria San Marcos tacos, Harlem’s delectable Charles Pan-Fried Chicken and bold Thai dishes from Farmhouse Kitchen. “…after attending 16 Coachellas, this behemoth, trendsetting music festival has rarely disappointed me and still manages to captivate, surprise, and evolve year after year despite the [few] names I know on the lineup,” In Spite Magazine wrote after attending last year’s edition. “If you’re open to a global soundscape with multiple genres on offer (or even just new musical experiences), Coachella is a value—not the horrendous, overblown, excessive, expensive nightmare people say it is.” To make sure you’re in the loop, our team has everything you need to know and more about Coachella 2026 below.
